fact: The 'Demon Star' — it winks every few days as an unseen companion eclipses it.
bio: Algol (Beta Persei) is a multiple system about 90 light-years away and the prototype of the eclipsing binary stars. Every 2.87 days a dimmer companion passes in front of the bright star, dropping its light noticeably for a few hours before it recovers.
cultural: The name is Arabic for 'the ghoul', and Algol marks the severed head of Medusa held by Perseus. Cultures from the Arab world to ancient Egypt seem to have marked this star's strange, regular 'winking' with unease long before its cause was understood.
